reviews.review:
Do you ever feel a strong desire to crush somebody's head with your bare hands?

Then you might like this game.

Well FINALLY! A decent take on a FPS Warhammer 40K! It looks great, feels great, moves great and is (depending on difficulty and/or single/multi-player game selection) as easy and/or hard as to be... - You guessed it: great!
The Story is simple and deep at the same time. Lots of shout-outs to the lore and the board game. There's a few things missing, but I'm gonna forgive it, simply because I understand the Devs' problem that they had to keep it all progressive and over-the-course-of-the-game-like. 
The graphics are so blocky and ugly that they're stunning. (Warhammer 40k fans will get what that means.)
The enemies and combat is in-your-face gory and brutal, as it should be in the deep dark universe of Warhammer 40k.The Arsenal of Weapons is not only cool, it stays true to the lore... The characters work incredibly well, and grow juuuust enough during the game that you're feelling bummed when it's all over. (SEQUEL!!! - I doubt it, but, I, for one, would welcome it.)
Right... So, down to cases.
Pros: 5/7 - Nice, simple, deep, developing, engaging storyline; decent, believable characters (I know you're hoping for more, Devs, but let's be honest. This is Warhammer 40k. Even decent and believable are BIG words of praise for story purposes.) ; Graphics are as they should be. Not pretty, but stunning in their dark, blocky, vast, gritty ugliness; Good Funfactor is excellent. Stomping, Chopping and Shooting Orks and Chaos Marines is SOOO much more fun than it sounds. And It actually gets harder and more fun in multiplayer once you take the time to get into it; Very Nice Replayabillity, (there's ton's of difference between single-and-multi-player-games, and the difference in difficulty settings-vs-feel in the campaign is visible enough that it makes several consecutive playthroughs viable.)
Cons: 2/7 The money-maker, unfortunately, is in effect in the multiplayer. (Look Devs, as much as I applaud you wanting to provide assistance to those unfortunate few who don't have the time, talent, skill, or dedication to "earn" the assorted skins, weapons, gadgets and-what-not, BUT do have REAL money they're willing to trade you to GIVE it to them isn't really endearing you to the rest of us, who like a challenge, who like to play and rank up and stuff. I understand you're running a business, I really do, but it's discouraging and more likely than not to make me quit the multiplayer than not.) ; Things are a liiiitle repetitious. The variation in topography and architecture makes it less obvious, and the progression in the singleplayer campaign to bigger, badder, better trained-and-equipped-enemies is all well and good, but while it IS fun to "SMITE THE INFIDELS" "FOR THE EMPEROR!" and all that, I'm not gonna lie. Sooner, rather than later, it'll get old. Thankfully there's tons of content and good ground for replayabillity here, but given the fact that competitors are already vying for top FPS spot in the Warhammer (40k and otherwise) theme, the Devs might wanna consider upping the ante on this title. Soon. More content... More Factions, (Guardsmen, Eldar, Tyranids?) maps, an expansion, whatever... - Theres room to grow here, people, and you know it.
(Oh. Incident'ly... I'm gonna go ahead and ask where the "Powers" are, in the game. You know... Psychers or whatever they were called in the boardgame... Every faction had them, more or less... They would probably rock the Multiplayer if you balanced them right... Just saying.)

Shoot and carve your way through hordes playing as a brutally stompy space marine. 

Easy to handle combat mechanics. Shooting and melee alternate smoothly.
(melee works a bit like dynasty warriors, 1-4 combo main attack with a stun/execution to close a combo off).

Masterful gameplay progression that changes pace just as sections settle into familiarity.

Weapons and vehicles from the franchise are shown in the best form to date, Bolters sound like the wrath of The Emperor familiar vehicles, buildings and architecture look better than even in Dawn of War (RTS) and every faction you see get models of high fidelity.

P.S.
Wrote this after the failure of a game space hulk: Deathwing was sent out to die as an inglorious, buggy, poor mans vermintide/L4D experience with lame (jar of jam in the face) spamtastic melee combat and gunplay that makes the original doom look advanced.
